page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per core. It lacks local storage and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for matrix multiplication acceleration.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-192 demonstrates top-tier multi-core processing capabilities, placing in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read operations. Single-core performance is comparatively moderate, with stress-ng single-core metrics falling into the average category, though Geekbench single-core and database operations remain strong. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for prompt processing on large 70B models and text generation on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density for parallelized workloads, delivering top-tier multi-threaded performance per resource unit. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. The instance is highly suitable for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, large-scale database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
